svg.title: The Hilbert insight: a divisibility ruler, not an orbit rule
svg.desc: Three panels: a Hilbert path labels a four-by-four grid; 18 and 1170 have matching base-four endings and orientation, hence matching local grid positions and powers-of-two fingerprints; their actual aliquot successors are 21 and 2106, with opposite parity. These two sources are being compared, not asserted to be consecutive orbit terms.
svg.text: An exact link between digits and geometry — not yet a rule for aliquot motion.
1 Fold the number line into a square
First digit 1: choose the blue quarter.
Each extra base-4 digit chooses one
of four smaller squares. Turns and
The digits are an address, not a factorization.
2 Matching endings preserve a geometric fingerprint
Same last 3 digits + same final orientation ⇒ same position modulo 8.
Different 8 × 8 tiles, shown aligned below. This does not mean nearby.
Both contain exactly seven factors of 2. Their sizes are NOT equal.
3 But that fingerprint does not predict the next term
Divisor sums see a distinction this digit-and-orientation summary lost.
This persists with arbitrarily many matching ending digits:
18 and 18(1 + 4^j), j ≥ 3, share state I and their last j digits,
but their aliquot successors have opposite parity.
An exact divisibility ruler — not yet an orbit rule.
This rejects a simple digit-state shortcut, not every Hilbert method. The conjecture remains open.
